items.title: Ebola response in eastern DR Congo must include food assistance, WFP says
items.desc: As Ebola sweeps across the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), ensuring families meet their basic food needs is crucial to halt the spread of the deadly disease.

items.title: ‘This is not 1945’: General Assembly president gavels open new session aimed at restoring global trust
items.desc: The UN General Assembly gavelled open its 81st session on Tuesday at UN Headquarters as the incoming president pledged to restore public trust in the institution during a time of war, humanitarian crises and intensifying climate change.

items.title: Syria’s transition hinges on justice for all, UN Human Rights Council hears
items.desc: A successful and lasting transition in Syria requires comprehensive accountability, inclusion and guarantees that violations will not be repeated, UN independent investigators told the Human Rights Council in Geneva on Tuesday.

items.title: In Gaza, women-headed households face ‘impossible choices’ to survive
items.desc: In war-torn Gaza, a growing number of women-headed households face “impossible decisions” every day, amid ongoing Israeli airstrikes and still-scarce resources, UN humanitarians said on Tuesday.

items.title: Tobacco use can undermine fertility, UN health agency warns
items.desc: Smoking very likely makes it harder to have a baby, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned in a new publication issued on Tuesday, highlighting that women who smoke have a 40 per cent higher risk of infertility compared to non-smokers.

items.title: US student visa issuances plunge 23% amid tighter immigration scrutiny
items.desc: The United States issued 23% fewer new student and exchange visas in 2025 compared to the previous year, driven by massive declines in approvals for applicants from India and China, according to newly released U.S. Department of State data.
